title: Spire and Garden
premise: Wren Iversen, a debt-bound scribe in the Spire's Ledger Guild, discovers that the guild's 'impossible things' are memories harvested from a sleeping god beneath the city — and that her own forgotten childhood was the first entry. When the border wards fall and the stars go out, Wren learns she carries the god's true name in her blood, a secret both the Spire and the exiled Garden cults will kill to control. Hunted across a darkened kingdom as the moon wanes toward its thirteenth turn, she must choose between restoring the god (and reigniting the ancient war) or erasing herself to keep the name buried. In the end, Wren splits the name among thousands of ordinary rememberers, freeing the god into fragments too small for any power to seize — at the cost of her own place in every ledger but one.
about_author: Petra Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed municipal records before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Wren Iversen, POV. A temple scribe deep in debt, Wren catalogs impossible acquisitions for the Ledger Guild: bottled laughter, a year of someone's grief. She notices an entry in her own handwriting she never wrote. Beat: unease planted beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. The border wards collapse and every star vanishes in one breath; panic floods the Spire. The Guildmaster orders all ledgers sealed, including Wren's anomalous entry. Beat: the ordinary world breaks open.

chapters.title: Sealed Stacks
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Sneaking into the sealed archive, she finds her missing years recorded as a Guild acquisition — sold by someone with her mother's signature. Beat: identity begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Debt
chapters.summary: Tam Vey, POV. A Garden courier caught stealing from the Guild offers Wren a trade: her true history for the ledger page naming her seller. Beat: temptation and distrust.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. An old priest explains the moon's thirteenth turn, when the sleeping god beneath the city can be named awake — or silenced forever. Wren realizes the name lives in her. Beat: dread of destiny.

chapters.title: Flight from the Spire
chapters.summary: Wren and Tam, alternating. The Guildmaster brands Wren a thief; they flee through starless streets as Guild hunters close in. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. Hiding in the flooded undercity, Tam reveals the Gardens were once the god's caretakers before the Spire enslaved it. Wren doubts everything she was taught. Beat: worldview inverted.

chapters.title: The First Entry
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Recovering a suppressed memory, Wren relives her mother selling her childhood to buy protection from the Guild. Grief and fury entwine. Beat: personal wound becomes the story's engine.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane, POV. Corvane, once idealistic, now believes only the Spire's controlled silence prevents war. He dispatches the Erasure, hunters who unmake memories. Beat: antagonist humanized, threat raised.

chapters.title: The Garden Gate
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Reaching the last free Garden, Wren meets its dying keeper, who confirms the name in her blood — and warns that waking the god means war. Beat: the choice takes shape.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Ash
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. Tam confesses he was sent to use Wren, not save her; their alliance shatters. Wren walks on alone. Beat: betrayal and loneliness at the lowest midpoint.

chapters.title: The Erasure Comes
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Hunters catch Wren; they begin stripping her memories, but the god's name burns them back, revealing her connection to it is alive, not archival. Beat: horror and strange empowerment.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. Corvane shows Wren the war the god's last waking caused — cities of ash he witnessed as a boy. His cruelty is conviction. Beat: stakes made morally symmetrical.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Escaping with Tam's unexpected return, Wren sees the moon nearing completion; factions mobilize — Spire loyalists, Garden zealots, opportunists. Beat: rising tide toward climax.

chapters.title: The Sleeping Deep
chapters.summary: Wren and Tam, alternating. Descending beneath the Spire, they reach the god's dreaming body, vast and sorrowful, half-harvested into ledgers. Beat: awe and pity.

chapters.title: Zealots at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. Garden extremists seize the descent, intending to force Wren to speak the name and weaponize the god. Tam turns against his own order. Beat: loyalty proven at cost.

chapters.title: The Name in Her Blood
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Cornered between Corvane's silence and the zealots' war, Wren understands neither side wants freedom — only ownership. Beat: clarity before the climax.

chapters.title: Moonfall
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. The thirteenth turn completes; the name rises to Wren's lips as Spire and Garden armies clash above. Beat: climax ignites.

chapters.title: Spoken and Shattered
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Instead of speaking the whole name, Wren shatters it into ten thousand syllables and releases them into the crowd below — each person carrying one fragment no army can collect. Beat: climactic sacrifice of singular power.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. The god stirs gently, distributed and harmless; Corvane's life's purpose collapses. He chooses, finally, not to erase Wren. Beat: antagonist's grace note.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Page
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Freed of debt but stripped from every official record, Wren finds her mother's grave and forgives what cannot be returned. Beat: mourning and release.

chapters.title: Garden, Growing
chapters.summary: Wren and Tam, alternating. Together they open a school where fragments are tended like seedlings, memory shared instead of owned. Wren writes one ledger of her own. Beat: hopeful, earned resolution.
